connectorUiConfig.title: QCrypton PQC Engine
connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown: The QCrypton PQC Engine data connector ingests runtime cryptographic telemetry from PQC Engine instances deployed on F5 BIG-IP into Microsoft Sentinel through the QCrypton API. PQC Engine is an OpenSSL 3.x provider that adds ML-KEM-768/1024 and ML-DSA-65/87 post-quantum algorithms. This connector streams handshake negotiations, KEM operations, policy enforcement events, and vulnerable algorithm detections into the PQCEngine_CL table.

sampleQueries.description: PQC adoption rate across handshakes in the last 24h
sampleQueries.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventType == 'handshake'
| summarize Total = count(), PQC = countif(PQCNegotiated == 1)
| extend PQCPct = round(100.0 * PQC / Total, 1)
| project Total, PQC, PQCPct

sampleQueries.description: Policy block events in the last 24h
sampleQueries.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventType == 'policy_block'
| project TimeGenerated, Hostname, InstanceId, Algorithm, NegotiatedGroup, CipherSuite, ClientClass, Detail
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where EventType == 'vuln_detected'
| summarize Count = count() by Algorithm, Detail
| order by Count desc

dataTypes.name: PQCEngine_CL
dataTypes.lastDataReceivedQuery:
PQCEngine_CL
| summarize Time = max(TimeGenerated)
| where isnotempty(Time)

instructionSteps.title: Connect QCrypton PQC Engine to Microsoft Sentinel

parameters.content: This connector polls the QCrypton PQC Engine API to retrieve runtime cryptographic telemetry and ingest it into the **PQCEngine_CL** table in your Log Analytics workspace.

#### 1. API Key
Obtain your QCrypton API key from the [QCrypton Portal](https://portal.qcrypton.com). Navigate to **Settings > API Keys** and generate a key with read access to engine telemetry.

#### 2. API Server URL
Enter the base URL of your QCrypton API server. The default is `https://api.qcrypton.com`. If you use a dedicated or regional instance, enter the URL provided by QCrypton.

parameters.label: QCrypton API Server URL
parameters.name: apiServerUrl
parameters.description: Enter the QCrypton API base URL. Do not include a trailing slash or path.

dataFlows.transformKql: source | extend TimeGenerated = iff(isnull(TimeGenerated), now(), TimeGenerated) | project TimeGenerated, InstanceId, Hostname, EventType, Algorithm, Operation, PeerGroups, NegotiatedGroup, CipherSuite, ClientClass, PQCOffered, PQCNegotiated, Success, Detail, Metadata

schema.name: PQCEngine_CL
schema.description: Runtime cryptographic telemetry from QCrypton PQC Engine instances deployed on F5 BIG-IP. Contains handshake negotiations, KEM/signature operations, policy enforcement events, vulnerable algorithm detections, and client classification.

columns.name: TimeGenerated
columns.description: Timestamp when the event was generated by the PQC Engine.

columns.name: InstanceId
columns.description: Unique identifier for the PQC Engine instance.

columns.name: EventType
columns.description: Event type: handshake, kem_op, sig_op, policy_block, policy_upgrade, vuln_detected, kex_complete.

columns.name: Algorithm
columns.description: Algorithm name e.g. mlkem768, mldsa65, RSA-2048.

columns.name: Operation
columns.description: Cryptographic operation: encapsulate, decapsulate, sign, verify.

columns.name: ClientClass
columns.description: Client classification: pqc_native, pqc_hybrid, classical, legacy.

columns.name: Metadata
columns.description: Additional JSON metadata about the event.

properties.displayName: [parameters('workbook1-name')]

properties.description: PolicyBlockDetected_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

The PQC Engine crypto policy enforcement blocked a TLS handshake that did not meet minimum
requirements. This may indicate a client attempting to connect with banned cipher suites,
blocked key exchange groups, or TLS versions below the policy minimum. Review the blocked
algorithm and client to determine if policy adjustment or client upgrade is needed.
properties.displayName: PQC Engine policy blocked a TLS handshake
properties.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "policy_block"
| project TimeGenerated, Hostname, InstanceId, Algorithm, NegotiatedGroup, CipherSuite, ClientClass, Detail
| order by TimeGenerated desc

properties.description: QCryptonPQCEngine Analytics Rule 1

properties.displayName: PQC Engine policy blocked a TLS handshake

properties.description: VulnerableAlgorithmDetected_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

The PQC Engine vulnerability database flagged a quantum-vulnerable algorithm during a TLS
handshake or cryptographic operation on F5 BIG-IP. Algorithms such as RSA-2048, ECDSA P-256,
or Ed25519 are vulnerable to Shor's algorithm on a cryptographically relevant quantum computer.
Migrate to PQ-hybrid algorithms (X25519+ML-KEM-768) to protect against harvest-now-decrypt-later
attacks.
properties.displayName: Vulnerable classical algorithm detected in TLS negotiation
properties.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "vuln_detected"
| project TimeGenerated, Hostname, InstanceId, Algorithm, Operation, ClientClass, PQCOffered, Detail
| order by TimeGenerated desc

properties.description: QCryptonPQCEngine Analytics Rule 2

properties.displayName: Vulnerable classical algorithm detected in TLS negotiation

properties.description: PQCDowngradeOnEngine_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

A TLS handshake completed where the client offered post-quantum hybrid key exchange groups but
the F5 BIG-IP negotiated a classical-only group. This may indicate PQC Engine misconfiguration,
an intermediate device stripping PQC groups from the ClientHello, or the engine running in
monitor mode rather than enforce mode. Investigate the negotiated vs offered groups.
properties.displayName: PQC downgrade on engine — client offered hybrid but classical negotiated
properties.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "handshake"
| where PQCOffered == 1 and PQCNegotiated == 0
| project TimeGenerated, Hostname, InstanceId, NegotiatedGroup, PeerGroups, CipherSuite, ClientClass, Detail
| order by TimeGenerated desc

properties.description: QCryptonPQCEngine Analytics Rule 3

properties.displayName: PQC downgrade on engine — client offered hybrid but classical negotiated

properties.description: HighClassicalClientRate_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

More than 50% of TLS handshakes on a PQC Engine instance in the last 24 hours were from
classical-only clients that did not offer any post-quantum key exchange groups. These
connections are not protected against harvest-now-decrypt-later attacks. Consider requiring
PQC-capable TLS libraries or upgrading connecting services to OpenSSL 3.5+ or BoringSSL with
ML-KEM support.
properties.displayName: High percentage of classical-only clients on PQC Engine
properties.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType == "handshake"
| summarize Total = count(), Classical = countif(ClientClass in ("classical", "legacy")) by Hostname, InstanceId
| extend ClassicalPct = round(100.0 * Classical / Total, 1)
| where ClassicalPct > 50
| project Hostname, InstanceId, Total, Classical, ClassicalPct
| order by ClassicalPct desc

properties.description: QCryptonPQCEngine Analytics Rule 4

properties.displayName: High percentage of classical-only clients on PQC Engine

properties.description: KEMOperationFailureSpike_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

An elevated rate of KEM (Key Encapsulation Mechanism) operation failures was detected on a
PQC Engine instance. This may indicate incompatible ML-KEM implementations between client and
server, corrupted key material, memory constraints on the F5 BIG-IP, or a misconfigured PQC
Engine provider. Investigate the failing algorithm and operation type.
properties.displayName: KEM operation failure spike on PQC Engine
properties.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
| where EventType == "kem_op"
| where Success == 0
| summarize FailureCount = count(), Algorithms = make_set(Algorithm, 5), Operations = make_set(Operation, 5) by Hostname, InstanceId
| where FailureCount > 5
| project Hostname, InstanceId, FailureCount, Algorithms, Operations
| order by FailureCount desc

properties.description: QCryptonPQCEngine Analytics Rule 5

properties.displayName: KEM operation failure spike on PQC Engine

properties.description: PolicyUpgradeActivity_AnalyticalRules Analytics Rule with template version 3.0.0

The PQC Engine policy engine upgraded the cipher selection for one or more TLS handshakes.
This occurs when the engine is in enforce mode and the initial negotiation would have used a
weaker algorithm than the policy allows. The engine intervened to select a stronger (typically
PQ-hybrid) algorithm. This is an expected and positive signal when enforcement is enabled.
properties.displayName: PQC Engine policy upgraded cipher selection
properties.query:
PQCEngine_CL
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where EventType == "policy_upgrade"
| summarize UpgradeCount = count(), Algorithms = make_set(Algorithm, 10) by Hostname, InstanceId
| project Hostname, InstanceId, UpgradeCount, Algorithms
| order by UpgradeCount desc

properties.description: QCryptonPQCEngine Analytics Rule 6

properties.displayName: PQC Engine policy upgraded cipher selection

properties.descriptionHtml:
Note: Please refer to the following before installing the solution:

• Review the solution Release Notes

• There may be known issues pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing.

Runtime cryptographic telemetry from QCrypton PQC Engine, an OpenSSL 3.x provider for F5 BIG-IP that adds ML-KEM-768/1024 and ML-DSA-65/87 post-quantum algorithms. Ingests handshake negotiations, KEM operations, policy enforcement events, vulnerable algorithm detections, and client classification into the PQCEngine_CL table via the Codeless Connector Framework (RestApiPoller). Ships with 1 data connector, 6 analytic rules, workbook, and Teams-notification playbook.

Underlying Microsoft Technologies used:

This solution takes a dependency on the following technologies, and some of these dependencies either may be in Preview state or might result in additional ingestion or operational costs:

• Microsoft Sentinel Codeless Connector Framework

Data Connectors: 1, Workbooks: 1, Analytic Rules: 6, Playbooks: 1
